title: Subtract the Product and Sum of Digits of an Integer
statement: Take the decimal digits of the positive integer `n`. Multiply all of them together, and separately add all of them up. Return the first result minus the second, that is (product of the digits) − (sum of the digits).
notes:
## Intuition

Everything depends on the digits, and the last digit of a number is `n % 10`. Dividing by 10 and dropping the remainder removes that digit, so repeating the two steps visits every digit from right to left. Keep a running product and a running sum along the way. Converting the number to a string and reading its characters would also work; the arithmetic loop avoids building that text.

## Approach

1. Start `product` at 1 (the empty product) and `sum` at 0.
2. While `n > 0`, take `digit = n % 10`.
3. Multiply `digit` into `product` and add it to `sum`.
4. Remove the digit with `n = Math.floor(n / 10)`.
5. Return `product - sum`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 234`. The first digit read is 4: `product = 4`, `sum = 4`, `n = 23`. Next 3: `product = 12`, `sum = 7`, `n = 2`. Last 2: `product = 24`, `sum = 9`, `n = 0`. The loop ends and the answer is `24 - 9 = 15`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(d), where d is the number of digits (at most 6 here).
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Start the product at 1, not 0, or it stays 0 forever.
- A single zero digit makes the product 0, so the answer is just `-sum` (for `10` it is `-1`).
- In JavaScript use `Math.floor(n / 10)`; plain `n / 10` keeps a fraction, so `n % 10` stops producing whole digits.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product` | product of the digits read so far |
| `sum` | sum of the digits read so far |
| `digit` | the current last digit of `n` |
| `n` | what is left of the number after removing read digits |

narration.2: An empty product is 1, so multiplying digits into it works from the start.
narration.5: Keep going while there are digits left.
narration.6: The remainder after dividing by 10 is the last digit.
narration.7: Multiply this digit into the running product.
narration.8: Add this digit to the running sum.
narration.9: Drop the last digit by dividing by 10 and rounding down.
narration.11: Every digit has been used; return product minus sum.
